newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Grande to reorganise Capetronic prior to KL list.
newsitem.headline: Grande to reorganise Capetronic prior to KL list.

text.p: The Grande Holdings Ltd announced it will restructure Capetronic Consumer Electronics Holdings Berhad (CCE) prior to its listing on the second board of the Kuala Lumpur stock exchange.

CCE, an investment holding company, was incorporated in Malaysia in May 1994 as a private limited company and converted to a public company in April 1996, Grande said in a statement published on Friday.
Grande currently has no holding in CCE, but has an attributable 71.25 percent interest in Capetronic (Malaysia) Corp Sdn Bhd (CMC) and Capetronic Consumer USA (HK) Ltd (CUL).
Following the restructuring, CCE will become a subsidiary of Grande and act as the holding company of CMC and CUL.
CMC and CUL will be the chief operating entities of the company to be listed.

In a series of transactions, Grande -- through another wholly owned subsidiary, Capetronics Consumer Electronics Holdings Ltd -- will acquire the 25 percent stakes held by independent Malaysian investors in CMC and CUL, and the stakes held by other Grande subsidiaries in CMC and CUL.
The entire issued share capital of CMC has been valued at 29.08 million ringgit (US$11.74 million).
The acquisition of the company will be satisfied with the issue of 25.73 million shares in CCE.
The entire issued share capital of CUL has been valued at 8.87 million ringgit ($3.8 million) and the acquisition will be satisfied with the issue of 7.85 million shares in CCE.
Grande directors expect to list CCE within the next eight to 10 weeks.
CCE would offer 10 million shares of 1.00 ringgit ($0.40) to the public. The net proceeds arising from the sale of shares in CCE by Grande would be about 31.2 million ringgit.
The proceeds from the new issue of shares in CCE, expected to be about 44.80 million ringgit, will be used to acquire land and build a new factory.
